title: A small depression on the maxillary palate
html: A 31-year-old woman was referred from a general dentistry practice to an oral and maxillofacial surgeon for evaluation of an incidental maxillary radiolucency noted on panoramic imaging (Figure 1). She had a history of anxiety disorder managed with duloxetine and reported taking naproxen and cyclobenzaprine. Her surgical history included a ganglion cyst removal without complications. She had no other significant medical history and reported no drug or food allergies. Social history included electronic-cigarette and occasional alcohol use.
